rationale.conceptual: The task involves constructing two atomic models (pristine Co-N4 and defect), running periodic DFT total-energy calculations for multiple adsorbate configurations, and applying the computational hydrogen electrode (CHE) model to compute working potentials. While these are standard methods in computational catalysis, they require understanding of periodic boundary conditions, pseudopotential selection, adsorption geometry optimization, and free-energy corrections. This is non-trivial but established, not a trivial textbook operation.
rationale.execution: The pipeline has only two explicit stages: DFT energy calculations (one block handling multiple sub-calculations) and a CHE post-processing step. The DFT runs are batchable and the post-processing is simple arithmetic. No complex orchestration, data fetching, or fragile multi-tool dependencies. With a single DFT code and standard scripting, this is a straightforward two-step engineering effort.
